scope_note: This checkpoint's PRIMARY finding is a ledger entry, not a harness: the program's stated minimal system for causal-net binding semantics (activity + input binding + output binding + marking -> enabled/refused -> next marking) is UNSUPPORTED ON BOTH SIDES. Confirmed by direct re-read of both codebases this checkpoint (not inherited from a prior audit round, which had mischaracterized the Lean side as having AND/XOR binding structure -- corrected here).

ledger_entries.claim: binding-set structure (AND/XOR obligations over specific target sets)

lean_side.finding: CausalBinding is a plain `{ sources: List alpha, targets: List alpha }` pair. No AND/XOR discriminant, no satisfaction predicate over specific target subsets.

rust_side.finding: Produces only a single AND/XOR string tag per node -- not a binding-set partition of which specific targets are jointly obligatory. Output is never consumed downstream (confirmed sole caller is the wasm-bindgen entry point, which just serializes it to JSON).

rust_side.note: independent hand-transcription of the literal formula, NOT wired to any production wasm4pm code path

ledger_entries.explicit_non_claim: This does NOT claim correspondence to wasm4pm::causal_graph::CausalRelation.strength. That field is a DIFFERENT formula: unsigned usize in [0,1000], with negative heuristic measures explicitly clamped to 0.0 via `.max(0.0)` before scaling (confirmed by direct read of build_causal_heuristic). Clamping a signed measure to zero before an affine rescale destroys the antisymmetry dependencyMeasure's own proof depends on -- these two are not the same claim under any honest normalization.
